**Image Analysis:**

- **Plant part affected**: Stem base and root system (two specimens shown)
- **Key visual features**:
  - Two stems with roots laid out, showing the base/soil-line region
  - Significant brown to dark brown discoloration of the stem tissue from the root zone upward
  - The inner/vascular tissue shows streaking brown discoloration longitudinally up the stem
  - Roots appear brown and damaged
  - No visible white mycelial mats (rules out Southern Blight, Sclerotinia)
  - No visible sclerotia (rules out Southern Blight, Sclerotinia Timber Rot)
  - No concentric ring pattern on stem cankers (makes Alternaria Stem Canker less likely)
  - Browning appears vascular in nature — darker streaking through internal stem tissue

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Verticillium_Wilt**: Classic diagnostic feature is brown vascular discoloration visible when stems are cut lengthwise — this image appears to show exactly that, with longitudinal brown streaking up from the root zone.
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**: Shows brown cankers at the base with vascular discoloration, possible — but bacterial streaming is the key indicator and not visible here.
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**: Requires dark, almost black cankers with concentric rings near soil line — the discoloration here is more diffuse brown, not clearly canker-like with rings.
- **Sclerotinia / Southern Blight**: Both require visible white mycelium and sclerotia — absent here.

The brown vascular streaking from the root zone up the longitudinal stem section is the hallmark of Verticillium_Wilt.
